title: Update User Flows
bottom_line: After changing your app in a session, run this command. It adds, revises and removes only the flows your changes touched, and never renumbers IDs.

sections.heading: Run it after you add, change or remove a feature

cards.title: An existing user-flows.md
cards.text: It needs a `user-flows.md` at the project root, made by `/user-flows:extract-user-flows`. If there is none, it stops and tells you to run that first.

cards.title: Changes in this session
cards.text: It looks at what was built, changed or removed in the current Claude Code session.

cards.title: Nothing else to install
cards.text: It needs nothing beyond Claude Code: it reads the code and writes `user-flows.md`. The plugin has no environment variables and no plugin settings.

blocks.text: Use it when you want to update, refresh or sync the user flows after implementing, changing or removing functionality. It is not for making flows from scratch.

blocks.title: Why it updates instead of starting over
blocks.text: The file feeds automated test generation, so outdated flows mean wrong tests. A full regeneration would change IDs that existing tests refer to, so this command changes only what it must.

sections.heading: It works out what changed from the chat and from git

nodes.label: The conversation: what was built or removed
Git: the diff and this session's commits
No behavior change: file left untouched

blocks.text: From git it reads `git diff` (unstaged and staged changes) plus any commits made during this session.

Nothing relevant means changes such as documentation only, or refactors where the behavior stays the same. It says so and leaves the file untouched, because a rewrite with no change in behavior only creates noise in the diff.

sections.heading: Each changed file is matched to flows through their Source line

rows: A file that appears in a flow's Source line
Claude checks that the flow's steps, precondition and expected outcome still match the code, and looks for new paths through the feature (see below).
A file that appears in no flow
It may be a new feature. Its flows are listed at the same granularity recorded in the file's header line.

blocks.title: New paths through an existing feature
blocks.text: A change can add a new path, such as a new validation branch, a new option, or a new error or permission case. Each one becomes a new flow if the file's granularity calls for it.
Every judgment is based on the code as it is now, not on what the diff appears to imply.
Each flow's Source line links that flow to the code that implements it, which is how changed files are matched to flows.

sections.heading: Only the touched flows change, and IDs never move

cards.title: Revised flow
cards.text: Keeps its ID. Only the fields that changed are updated: steps, precondition, expected or source.

cards.title: New flow
cards.text: Gets the next ID after the highest one, under the matching area heading. The heading is created if the area is new.

cards.title: Removed flow
cards.text: Its entry is deleted. Nothing else is renumbered, and its ID is never reused.

cards.title: Duplicate of an existing flow
cards.text: A new flow with the same steps and outcome as an existing one, differing only in data values, is merged into the existing entry instead of added.

cards.title: Untouched flows
cards.text: Stay exactly as they were, with no reformatting, reordering or rewording, so the file's diff shows only what changed in behavior.

cards.title: Header line
cards.text: The `generated:` date is updated. Granularity and area stay as they were.

blocks.text: Every flow it writes follows the same definitions as `/user-flows:extract-user-flows`: what a user flow is, the granularity levels, the rules against duplicates and the exact entry format.

sections.heading: When any flow changed, the tests are synced too

blocks.text: After writing the file, Claude runs `/user-flows:test-user-flow`. The test sync acts only on the flows this update touched and leaves the rest of the test suite alone. It is skipped when the file was left untouched.
If the project has no user-flow tests yet and you have not asked for them, Claude mentions that `/user-flows:test-user-flow` can generate them.

sections.heading: The report lists every added, revised and removed flow

cards.title: Added
cards.text: The IDs and names of new flows.

cards.title: Revised
cards.text: The IDs of changed flows and what changed in each.

cards.title: Removed
cards.text: The IDs and names of removed flows. Removed IDs are listed explicitly, because tests that refer to them need to be deleted or updated.

cards.title: Test sync
cards.text: The outcome of the test sync, if it ran.

blocks.caption: It does not paste the whole file back into the conversation.

next_action.text: After you implement, change or remove functionality in a session, run `/user-flows:update-user-flows`.
next_action.detail: If it says there is no user-flows.md, run `/user-flows:extract-user-flows` first.
